title: Kollab
subtitle: Capabilities and guided practice
body: A working handbook for authors, reviewers, and administrators
notes: Introduce the course as a guided exploration of the restored Kollab team. The team includes Features, Technical Implementation, and Training & Workshops. This is sample documentation, not production data. Suggested duration: 60–75 minutes. Open the team handbook before starting.

title: The learning path
body: Find and organize knowledge
Write with useful rich content
Collaborate, review, and recover
Understand the implementation
notes: Ask participants which role they play: author, reviewer, administrator, or developer. Explain that the deck introduces a workflow, then the handbook provides the detailed instructions. Reserve time for the three workshops. Use the Features project to orient the audience.

title: Teams, projects, and pages
left: Projects group a body of work.
right: Features and Technical Implementation form the handbook.
notes: Show the Teams directory, open Kollab, and switch between its three projects. Expand a page tree. Explain personal spaces separately: they support an individual's content; this package demonstrates team and project scope. Avoid treating the hierarchy as the complete permissions model.

title: Finding the right page
body: Search accessible content by keyword.
Browse a page index when you know the title.
Use tags and properties to find related pages.
notes: Open Knowledge directory and compare the page index with the Area properties report. The report has real indexed rows in the archive. Semantic search needs a compatible configured embedding provider; do not imply that search enrichment is always available. Have a participant find the recovery instructions.

title: Reading and editing
right: Insert blocks with the toolbar or slash menu.
Configure macros at the point of use.
notes: Open Rich authoring demonstration. Switch between Read and Edit. Show slash-command discovery on an empty paragraph and dismiss it without changing the page. Explain that visible controls depend on access, and the server still enforces permissions.

title: Rich content with a purpose
notes: Use the authoring demonstration page and explain why each block appears. Change an inline status label, then point out that this does not change the page's governance review state. Use one task checkbox. Status and date chips can be configured in Edit mode.

title: Layouts for different reading paths
body: Headings and a table of contents support scanning.
Details hide optional explanation until needed.
Tabs separate perspectives; columns compare related ideas.
notes: Expand the milestone explanation. Switch Author, Reviewer, and Operator tabs. Scroll to the two-column comparison. Ask whether each layout makes the page easier to use. Emphasize that plain prose remains appropriate for most explanations. Check narrow-screen readability if presenting mobile use.

title: Diagrams beside the explanation
code:
flowchart LR
  Client --> API
  API --> Database
body: Mermaid stores diagram source in the page.
The live example shows Kollab's deployment.
Visual editors provide optional drawing workflows.
notes: Open Architecture walkthrough, then inspect a Mermaid block in Edit mode. Explain that the small source sample on this slide is illustrative. Draw.io loads an external editor; Excalidraw uses a bundled component. The integration-boundaries page has clearly labeled blank canvases for practice.

title: Reusable knowledge
left: Define an excerpt on a source page.
Keep its identity stable when editing.
right: Create a page from a template.
notes: Open Reusable knowledge and show the included product description from the team handbook. Compare it with the Technical decision template and Validation note snippet. Explain that a template is starting content and does not synchronize later edits into existing pages.

title: Properties turn pages into a collection
body: A page-properties block stores key/value metadata.
The save path maintains a queryable index.
A properties report groups accessible pages by that metadata.
notes: Inspect the Area, Audience, and Availability properties on a feature page. Return to the report. The source document is authoritative; the normalized index makes cross-page queries practical. Ask participants to name a useful property for their own workspace.

title: Files and presentations
body: Attach a file to the page that explains it.
Use an attachment list or a single-file block.
Download the original; preview it when the service supports it.
notes: Open the training materials page and download this PowerPoint. Show the Markdown instructor guide beside it. Office previews require the media-preview service; downloading does not depend on successful preview generation. Image libraries provide a separate workflow for reusable images.

title: Collaborative work
body: Live editing keeps accepted page changes synchronized.
Comments preserve discussion beside the content.
Assigned tasks make follow-up work visible.
notes: Use separate workshop accounts for a two-person demonstration. Open the sample comment thread and identify it as illustrative. Show the task assigned to the demo administrator. Task extraction currently recognizes textual @username content; the sample includes that explicit assignee alongside a user mention. Avoid implying that one shared account demonstrates distinct user presence.

title: Review, publishing, and history
notes: Explain the distinctions before demonstrating. Open the content-review block and History on Collaboration laboratory. Point to Training baseline. The sample review state is in review; it does not claim a real approval. Publishing and restoration are actions with separate effects; use a practice page for mutations.

title: Access follows the resource
body: Team and project roles establish space access.
Page restrictions can narrow access to content.
The server checks the caller for each protected operation.
notes: Open the access guide. Explain that navigation visibility is not the security boundary. Show page restrictions only on a practice page. Sharing links are separate capabilities with their own scope and settings. Do not use the publicly known source content to infer that restored pages are anonymously readable.

title: Three different recovery operations
notes: This is a critical distinction for administrators. The delivered demonstration archive uses the full-server restore path and must go into a fresh or intentionally disposable target. It does not merge a team into an existing workspace. Explain that full sync preserves unrelated destination data while full restore replaces it.

title: The backup package
body: Database rows use kollab.database.v2.
Uploaded bytes travel with their metadata.
Restore checks the schema and migration ledger.
notes: Explain that the archive contains PostgreSQL rows serialized into JSON, not SQLite and not a SQL dump. The export excludes installation-specific coordination state. The ZIP includes a generated demo administrator account; its password is supplied privately beside the artifact. Restore invalidates editor state.

title: Application architecture
left: Tiptap and Yjs support structured collaboration.
Go handlers and services enforce behavior.
right: An uploads filesystem holds file bytes.
notes: Switch to the full Mermaid architecture diagram in Technical Implementation. Follow one document read through the API to PostgreSQL, then an attachment read to uploads. The browser never connects directly to the database. Office conversion is an additional service, not part of the editor process.

title: The editor's data contract
body: Registered nodes define valid document structure.
Atom macros use typed configuration.
Derived indexes support reports and tasks.
notes: Open Document model and macro contracts. This minimal sample shows the storage shape, not a complete property example. Explain native container nodes versus atom macroBlock nodes. The showcase validates its generated documents against the actual editor schema so unsupported node names fail verification.

title: Optional services and prototypes
notes: State exactly which services are available in the workshop environment. No live provider credentials are included in this archive. Confluence archive migration is implemented, but a live Confluence embed is not exposed in the current UI. Do not treat historical design documents as evidence that planned controls are delivered.

title: Guided practice
body: Build a technical page with purposeful macros.
Review a change and inspect a named checkpoint.
Trace page properties from the editor to PostgreSQL.
notes: Open the three workshop pages in Training & Workshops. Participants can complete the first two without reading source code. Developers can use the third to trace a feature across layers. Encourage participants to create their own practice pages so generated source pages remain easy to compare with Git.

title: Maintaining the handbook
body: Edit guides, design references, and curated source pages in Git.
Regenerate the pages and training deck.
Verify the archive, then rehearse in a fresh instance.
notes: Explain the one-way publication workflow. Editing a restored page does not update Git automatically. Copy intentional changes back to the appropriate source. Stable source keys preserve page IDs. Rebuild after schema changes; never change the migration ledger to force an incompatible restore. Generated passwords and archive ZIPs stay out of Git.

title: Ready to use Kollab
body: Create a page another person can use.
Choose a macro because it helps the reader.
Know the scope before changing access or restoring data.
notes: Ask each participant to demonstrate one workflow from the readiness checklist. Suggested questions: Does a status badge approve a page? Does restoring this archive merge a team? What service is required for Office previews? End by pointing to the maintained Features and Technical Implementation projects for continued learning.
